exposure: Type of therapy during pregnancy (surgery, chemotherapy)
outcome: Child condition at 1-year follow-up (growth, development, complications)
cohort: The study included 84 pregnant women diagnosed with malignant tumors during pregnancy between 2001 and 2022.
finding: Most children of mothers with cancer had a favorable condition at birth and at 1-year follow-up, and maternal survival rates were high, with factors like applying therapy during pregnancy, no malignancy progression, later gestational week delivery, lower histopathological grade, surgery, higher birthweight, and cesarean section predicting favorable 1-year outcomes.
mod_finding: Delivery by cesarean section was identified as a predictor of favorable 1-year condition for children.
birth_weight: Birth weight was measured, and obtaining higher birthweight was identified as a predictor for favorable 1-year condition of children.
gest_age: Average gestational age at delivery was 33.01 ± 6.16 weeks (range: 20-40 weeks), and delivery at a later gestational week was a predictor for favorable 1-year maternal condition.
